## Figure 2.1: Global Uncertainty amid Successive Shocks
Type: line chart

- **Units:** Index (2000 = 100)
- **Y-axis:** Index, from **0 to 1,200**; labeled ticks at **0, 100, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1,000, 1,200**
- **X-axis:** Years from **2000 to 2026**, labeled at **2000, 2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, 2025**
- **Time span:** **2000 to 2026Q2**
- **Series / legend:**
  - **World Uncertainty Index** (dark blue)
  - **Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index** (light blue)
- **Reference line:** dashed horizontal line at **100**

### Approximate values and visually identifiable points

Because the chart does not print point labels, all values below are estimated from line positions.

#### World Uncertainty Index (dark blue)
- **2000:** ≈80–100
- **2001:** rises to ≈150–250
- **2002:** ≈120–280
- **2003:** local spike ≈370
- **2004–2007:** mostly ≈110–180, with a brief rise around **2006–07** to ≈230
- **2008–2011:** generally ≈140–240
- **2012:** sharp rise to ≈400, then ≈280
- **2013:** peak around ≈420, then falls toward ≈180
- **2014:** ≈180–220
- **2015:** spike ≈320, then ≈250
- **2016:** ≈180–260
- **2017:** peak ≈340
- **2018:** ≈160–300
- **2019:** rises to ≈420–440
- **2020:** major surge to ≈570–600
- **2021:** falls sharply to ≈130, then rebounds toward ≈280
- **2022:** ≈260–320
- **2023:** ≈280–320
- **2024:** declines to ≈170–200
- **2025:** extreme spike to **≈1,150** (chart maximum)
- **2026Q2:** falls back but remains very high at **≈850–900**

#### Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index (light blue)
- **2000:** ≈70–90
- **2001:** ≈100–150
- **2002:** spike ≈250
- **2003:** ≈120–230
- **2004–2007:** mostly ≈70–110
- **2008–2009:** jump to ≈150–280, then around ≈140–180
- **2010–2011:** ≈140–180
- **2012:** spike ≈280, then ≈180–220
- **2013–2016:** mostly ≈140–190
- **2017:** rises to ≈300
- **2018:** ≈180–240
- **2019:** increases to ≈260–380
- **2020:** around ≈250–350
- **2021:** spike to ≈520, then around ≈300–450
- **2022:** ≈220–330
- **2023:** ≈260–400
- **2024:** ≈200–310
- **2025:** surges to **≈830**
- **2026Q2:** remains elevated around **≈380–600**

### Rankings and comparisons
- The **largest value in the figure** is the **World Uncertainty Index** peak in **2025** at **≈1,150**.
- The **second-largest major spike** is the **Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index** in **2025** at **≈830**.
- The **smallest values** for both series occur near the start of the sample, around **2000**, at roughly **≈70–100**.
- The **World Uncertainty Index** is generally more volatile and reaches higher peaks than the **Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index**.
- Around **2020**, the **World Uncertainty Index** peaks higher (≈600) than the **Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index** (generally below ≈400 at that point).
- Around **2021**, the **Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index** briefly exceeds the **World Uncertainty Index** because the latter drops sharply after its 2020 peak.
- In **2025–2026**, both series rise dramatically, but the **World Uncertainty Index** climbs much higher and remains above the policy uncertainty index at the end of the period.

### Trends
- Both series start near the **100** rebased benchmark in **2000**.
- Both show repeated spikes associated with successive shocks over the period.
- There are notable surges in the early **2000s**, around **2008–09**, **2012–13**, **2017–20**, **2021**, and especially **2025**.
- The most dramatic movement is the surge after **2024**, culminating in record highs in **2025**, followed by only partial retracement by **2026Q2**.
- Throughout most of the period after 2008, both indices remain frequently above the **100** baseline.

**Sources:** Original calculations based on data from the World Uncertainty Index database and the Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index database.

**Note:** The World Uncertainty Index measures broad uncertainty using Economist Intelligence Unit country reports. The Global Economic Policy Uncertainty Index measures uncertainty around economic policy using newspaper coverage and is aggregated across 20 economies using current price GDP weights. Both series are rebased so that their average value in 2000 equals 100. Data shown through 2026Q2.
